stances.claim: True collegiality means disagreeing without being disagreeable and differing without being difficult -- because the disagreement is with views and thoughts, not with persons or with comradeship.
stances.rhetorical_move: collegiality-as-disposition framing (defining institutional harmony by intellectual independence)

stances.claim: Filipinos at retired-justice age (well past the national average of 70) live on 'bonus days' granted by the Lord; the appropriate response is daily thanksgiving and intentional living, not regret about the past.
Snoopy is right and Charlie Brown is wrong: 'We only die once. We live every day' -- meaning each additional day is the unit of moral attention, not 'one life.'
stances.rhetorical_move: cartoon-aphorism-as-philosophy (using popular culture to convey existential framing)

stances.claim: Within 25 years, the convergence of 5G, AI, cryptocurrencies, IoT and especially stem-cell regenerative medicine will make natural-cause death 'optional' for the grandchildren of today's seniors -- humans will routinely live to 150 by growing or trading replacement body parts.
stances.rhetorical_move: near-future-extrapolation (treating laboratory telomere experiments as foreshadowing of routine human practice)

notable_anecdotes: The Snoopy-Charlie-Brown cartoon -- gifted via Viber, used as the philosophical centerpiece of the talk; 'We only die once. We live every day' has become a quotable CJ-favored aphorism.

The 1950s/60s Manila nostalgia inventory -- 15-centavo bus fares on Halili Transit and JD Bus, four pesos to the dollar, dating at Moonlit Terrace, Jai Alai Sky Room and Winter Garden, and singers like Pilita Corrales -- used to bond with fellow seniors via shared period reference.
The university-belt law school roll call (UP, Ateneo, USC, UST, San Beda, MLQ, UE, FEU) -- invoking the now-traffic-laden alma maters of his cohort.

The futurist arc -- 5G smartphone shopping, monitored home CCTV from abroad, AI, cryptocurrencies, IoT, stem-cell body-part replacement, telomere lengthening -- wrapped up with 'death from disease will be optional' in 25 years.

The Einstein-vs-bar-flunker brain auction joke -- Einstein's brain at $1,000 because it's overused, the flunker's brain at $100,000 because it's 'almost new and underused' -- the most quotable CJ humor moment of the column.
The closing 'Mabuhay!' -- CJ's recurring signature Filipino valedictory.

one_paragraph_summary: In a Christmas-season column summarizing his talk to retired SC justices at their Christmas party, Panganiban offers a meditation on collegiality, gratitude, nostalgia, and futurism. He opens with his canonical formula for principled disagreement -- 'disagree without being disagreeable... differ without being difficult' -- and explains why lay people are surprised that justices remain the best of colleagues after strongly worded opposing opinions: the disagreement is with views, not with persons. He thanks God for the 'bonus days and years' beyond the Philippine average longevity of 70 (69 men, 71 women), citing a Snoopy-Charlie-Brown cartoon -- 'We only die once. We live every day' -- and exhorts seniors to make each day count: 'Smile, laugh, sing, dance, help the poor, enjoy life... till we reach 100 and beyond.' He indulges generational nostalgia -- 1950s university-belt law schools (UP, Ateneo, USC, UST, San Beda, MLQ, UE, FEU), 15-centavo bus fares on Halili Transit and JD Bus, four pesos to the dollar, dates at Moonlit Terrace and Jai Alai Sky Room, and the singers Sylvia La Torre, Ruben Tagalog, Diomedes Maturan and Pilita Corrales -- and pivots to the futurist arc: 5G smartphone shopping and home CCTV, AI, cryptocurrencies, IoT, and the stem-cell revolution that will let grandchildren live 150 years via grown or traded replacement body parts. 'Death from disease will be optional' in 25 years; aging will be reversed via telomere lengthening, already shown possible in lab experiments. He closes with the trademark Einstein-vs-bar-flunker brain auction joke (Einstein's brain is cheaper because it's already overused) and his signature Filipino valedictory: 'Mabuhay!'
